rationale: Pulling the two November lots forward and routing the three later lots direct removes all USD 227K of duty for about USD 12K. Routing all five lots direct is USD 2K cheaper but means rebooking the WO-2604 inlet panels inside four weeks of dispatch, with only 6 days of float if the new booking slips. The 2025 aerostructures tariff (PRE-07) was solved the same way, and its lesson holds here: the exposure comes from US bonded transit, not origin.

qa.answer: Four options. Pull the November lots forward and route the rest direct (USD 12K, no duty, recommended), route all five unshipped lots direct (USD 10K, no duty, more rebooking risk on the WO-2604 lot), pull forward only and pay duty on the three later lots (USD 90K), or absorb the full USD 227K and move 2027 buys to Prairie Composites.

Routing all five unshipped lots direct EU to SIN is cheapest at about USD 10K and avoids the duty entirely. It needs Rhone Acoustique to hand the WO-2604 inlet panels to a new booking within four weeks of dispatch. The recommended mix costs USD 2K more and keeps that lot on its existing booking.

In 2025 a tariff change hit EU aerostructures routed via US facilities, including Rhone Acoustique panels (PRE-07). We pulled shipments ahead of the effective date and routed the rest direct EU to SIN for USD 46K, avoiding duty on 80% of the volume with no delay. The lesson was to check routing first, because most exposure came from US bonded transit rather than origin.

No induction moves. WO-2604 needs 4 inlet panels from PO 4500018351-00010 at its 6 Nov induction in nacelle cell N-02, and they land 6 Nov with 6 days of float to absorb the 2 to 4 day classification holds. The risk on this signal is cost, not schedule.
